heroLead: Hughesville sits along Muncy Creek in Lycoming County, in a dry-gas Marcellus corridor that's been developed since the play's earliest years.
intro: Hughesville is a Lycoming County borough along Route 405 and Muncy Creek, in one of the most consistently developed dry-gas counties in the entire Marcellus play. Families with land here often have leases and production history going back well over a decade.
We buy mineral and royalty interests near Hughesville, whether producing, leased and undeveloped, or a fractional share from inherited farmland.

sections.heading: Lycoming County's long development history
paragraphs: This part of the county has seen consistent dry-gas development for years, which generally means Hughesville-area tracts have real production history to evaluate rather than undeveloped speculative acreage.

sections.heading: What a mature royalty statement can tell you
paragraphs: A well with a decade or more of statements shows its actual decline pattern clearly, which gives a much better basis for valuing an interest than a projection on a newer well.

sections.heading: How we approach an offer
paragraphs: We review lease terms, production trend, and current deductions on your statement before naming a figure, and explain our reasoning.

We're happy to explain exactly how your well's decline curve factored into the number we're offering. We're also glad to explain how Muncy Creek corridor development compares to the rest of Lycoming County, since local density can differ meaningfully from the county-wide picture.

faqs.question: Is Hughesville in a strong part of the Marcellus dry-gas play?
faqs.answer: Yes, Lycoming County has been one of the most consistently developed dry-gas counties in the play, and Hughesville-area acreage generally has real production history to evaluate.

faqs.question: My Hughesville-area well has been producing for over a decade. Does that make it more or less valuable?
faqs.answer: It depends on where the well sits on its decline curve — a mature well typically produces less than it did early on, which we factor into valuation based on your actual recent statements.

faqs.question: What documents help most for a Hughesville-area review?
faqs.answer: Recent royalty statements are the most useful, showing current production and terms directly, though we can also work from a lease or parcel description.

faqs.question: Do older Hughesville-area leases from the first Marcellus wave have different deduction language than newer ones?
faqs.answer: Often, yes — leases negotiated in the earliest years of the play sometimes have less favorable post-production deduction language than leases signed later once landowners had more negotiating leverage, so we read each one individually.
